newsitem.title: USA: D.C. panel orders $85.6 million in FY '97 cuts.
newsitem.headline: D.C. panel orders $85.6 million in FY '97 cuts.

text.p: The District of Columbia's financial control board Friday ordered the city to slash $85.6 million in fiscal year 1997 to prevent the city from exceeding a spending cap set by Congress.
The five-member control board, however, did not spell out how many jobs Mayor Marion Barry and agency officials must cut.
"We did not identify the number of reductions. We fully anticipate some reductions must be made," control board chairman Andrew Brimmer said.

The control board outlined several areas for cuts, including a $16.2 million reduction in the annual budget of the University of the District of Columbia and $8 million in reductions in summer youth and youth violence programs.
The control board also ordered the city to cut $9 million in administrative services, $1 million in subsidies to the D.C. General Hospital and $8 million in spending for corrections services.
The panel ordered the city to save $5.4 million by reducing overtime payments to D.C. workers and to cut police department full-time employees by $1.4 million.
The control board issued the order as the White House considered options for helping the city deal with a multi-billion dollar financial crisis.
